V. ALTERNATIVES
A. Not to Improve This Highway Facility
In brief, leaving the existing roadway without improvement would lead to increasing congestion and a reduced level of service as traffic volumes increase. With this would be the associated increase in accident rates, noise, air pollution, operating costs and impairment of access to abutting land and communities. This, in the long run, would lead to a reduction in the quality of the environment and would not comply with the goals and objectives of the transportation and local plans.
B. To Improve This Highway Facility
Relocating the improvement either north or south of the present Lincoln Highway location would pose severe problems. Extensive right-of-way takings would be required.
Furthermore, Lincoln Highway presently acts as a natural neighborhood and school attendance boundary and any major change in its location would be disruptive to established community life.
Interstate Route 80 has been constructed to the north of Lincoln Highway and there is a proposed east-west freeway under study in a corridor several miles to the south. The eastern terminus of the proposed improvement is controlled by a newly completed improvement from Chicago Road eastward through the City of Chicago Heights.
To the west, the location of the improvement is fixed by the recently constructed interchange between Lincoln Highway and Interstate Highway 57 and the presently improved intersection of Lincoln Highway and Cicero Avenue.
These considerations and the extensive residential and commercial developments, long established in the area through which this improvement will pass, have limited the location of this improvement to the existing corridor. The study considered how best to accommodate the highway improvement largely within the existing right-of-way with as little land taking and disruption to business and neighborhood values as possible while improving alignment, increasing safety and adding the traffic capacity required for the design year of 1990.
Alternate alignments (designated "A" and "B") considered for this improvement were located to make optimum use of the existing right-of-way. A four-lane facility is proposed for that portion east of Western Avenue and a six-lane facility for that portion west of Western Avenue. Additional turning lanes are provided at intersections, as required. Generally, the centerline of the improved highway is located on the centerline of the present and proposed right-of-way, thus equalizing to a great extent the taking of private property north and south of the improvement. However, in two locations existing features required other alignments. Existing topographic features and facilities were disturbed as little as possible.
